research/autonomy/research-ledger.json — AUT-PD-171 RAISED to 130.0, its existing basis preserved and the raise appended. ⛔ THE SCORE RESTORATION ITSELF WAS NOT THIS CYCLE'S WORK AND IS NOT CLAIMED AS IT. This cycle hit the same second trunk red independently (origin/main carrying 74 open unscored rows against the ratchet's 73, blocking its commit) and diagnosed the same cause — ba12a1f8a nulling the score on a row `priority.py` cannot re-derive, because inheritance needs a route row in systems/graph and RT-AUTONOMY has none. But while this cycle was in its ~13.5-minute gate, two other cycles landed the fix on the trunk (620280791, d45067c00), restoring 120.0. That restoration stands untouched. What this cycle adds is the RAISE, on evidence the restoration did not have: occurrences four and five of the id collision, both measured live here. ⚠ THREE SESSIONS diagnosed one trunk red within the same hour without being able to see each other — the same duplicated-effort pattern CLAUDE.md §7 records for AUT-PD-160, reproduced exactly.
finding: ⛔⛔ THE TRUNK WAS RED AND NOTHING WAS LOOKING AT IT. `main` had been failing since b01f1843f (AUT-PD-167): 5 of 10,888 modalities tests, all in one file. Root cause taken as an observation rather than a reading of the diff — the same file gives `12 passed` in a detached worktree at b01f1843f^ and `5 failed, 7 passed` at ef3fe1a8b. AUT-PD-167 pinned MEMBERSHIP_SOURCE to `curated_only`, so `member_z()` returns {} by design and `panel_membership_source` re-keys off the pin; the five assertions are the pre-pin contract verbatim. ⭐ THE CLASS IS THE FINDING, NOT THE FAILURE. b01f1843f DID write a guard for the behaviour it introduced — test_the_panel_read_is_pinned_not_inherited.py, 180 lines, same commit — and never touched the guard for the behaviour it replaced. Seventh instance of the one-of-a-pair defect in this repository, and the second filed on 2026-08-29 alone (AUT-PD-171 is the same shape). ⚠ AND THE COMMIT LOOP COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT, BY DESIGN: the modalities suite left preflight on 2026-08-25, so b01f1843f's own preflight was green and correct. tests.yml is the authority and it went red on schedule. The accepted trade in CLAUDE.md §6 worked exactly as written — with nobody reading the result for the whole interval. ⛔⛔ THE SIXTH DEFECT, WHICH THE FIVE FAILURES WERE HIDING, IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. `test_gene_reads_wins_where_both_sources_carry_a_gene` asserted only `readable_pool == 8`, and that counts GENES — it is 8 whichever source wins, since the set is identical and only the values differ. A mutation deleting the precedence outright SURVIVED it, in the original file as much as in the rewrite: the test's name and docstring claimed a value invariant while its assertion checked set membership. The invariant was unobservable because the merge was inline in `build()`, so it is now a named function and the test asserts the values. Mutation set: 4 of 5 caught before, 5 of 5 after. ⛔⛔ AND A SECOND TRUNK RED, IN A DIFFERENT GATE, FOUND ONLY BECAUSE IT BLOCKED THIS COMMIT. `origin/main` carries 74 open unscored ledger rows against the AUT-PD-145 ratchet's pinned 73, so gate 13 is red on the trunk too — a second red nobody was reading, in the suite that DOES run in the commit loop. Cause: ba12a1f8a nulled AUT-PD-171's score expecting the scorer to re-derive it, and on an RT-AUTONOMY row a nulled score is a silent deletion. ⚠ THE TWO REDS SHARE A SHAPE WORTH NAMING: in both, a cycle changed one half of a coupled pair — a contract without its guard, a score without the deriver that would restore it — and the gate that would have caught it fires later, in someone else's commit loop. ⚠ AND THE TWO DEFECTS FILED HERE COMPOUND, WHICH THIS CYCLE PAID FOR TWICE. `ids.next_entry_id` collides (AUT-PD-171) and gate 13 now costs ~13.5 minutes (AUT-PD-183), so the collision window is not the derivation instant but the whole gate: this cycle derived AUT-PD-178, lost it, renumbered to AUT-PD-179, gated again, and lost that too. The second collision was caught only by an explicit pre-check written into this cycle's own conflict resolver — a plain rebase would have produced a ledger with two AUT-PD-179s, which `priority.py` refuses to rank.
what_it_cost: $0. CPU only: one Actions read, one detached worktree, ten mutation runs of a 12-test file, one artifact --check, and FIVE preflight runs — one invalidated by a concurrent push, one red on the trunk's own ratchet, three lost to push races. At ~13.5 min each (AUT-PD-183) that is over an hour of wall clock in gates, against a trunk committing every 2–5 minutes. ⛔ THAT RATIO IS THE REPORTABLE NUMBER: a gated commit loop longer than the trunk's inter-commit interval cannot converge by rebasing, and this cycle lost the race three times in a row before landing.
